summary:
Today's biggest story by far is the FDA's class-wide NAION (rare optic-nerve vision loss) warning, announced 9 Nov. It covers tirzepatide, semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide and orforglipron. Every major US and UK outlet has run it, and "ozempic blindness" is trending in Google GB with 1,000+ searches. Mainstream news has peaked, but calm, numbers-first explainers aimed at people already on tirzepatide are still thin. Most coverage leads with "blindness". The real numbers are reassuring in absolute terms. In the FDA meta-analysis of 126 RCTs (134,253 patients), the rate was 6.4 per 100,000 person-years on GLP-1 medicines vs 3.8 on comparators. Sentinel found no significant rise vs SGLT-2 inhibitors. This is our best opportunity this week: lead Shorts today, plus an evergreen label-based long-form, "Tirzepatide and Your Eyes".

Second: a new Nature Medicine RCT (9 Nov). In 120 adults on tirzepatide, resistance training three times a week for 40 weeks meant about 25% less lean-mass loss than usual activity, with 91% adherence. It's fresh randomized data, only UWA has a press release so far, and creator coverage is almost nil. It's a narrow, adjacent hook for the stalled Strength video, not another general protein video.

Third: Lilly's ATTAIN-OSA results for orforglipron in sleep apnea (9 Nov) and two retatrutide knee osteoarthritis Phase 3s (8 Nov). Both suit the 13:00 lead Short.

Upcoming: ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov) should bring the full REDEFINE 4 data, CagriSema vs tirzepatide. It's randomized and open-label, which is the only kind of news allowed as an extra L2 if it's made public within 48 h.

The playbook's Lane A evergreen queue is all still valid, and several items get seasonal hooks. Thanksgiving peaks 18–27 Nov. Holiday drinks give alcohol a hook, flu season gives dehydration and sick days one, and big meals give burping and heartburn one. Injection site reactions, keeping results after stopping, and burping and heartburn stay strong.

I rated these as caution: the semaglutide sheep pregnancy study (animal-only), gray-market "research-use" tirzepatide vials (at most 1 Short a week), and the thyroid review. Anything about buying or sourcing these medicines is rejected.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the FDA's new NAION eye warning: what the label change means, the absolute risk (6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years in 126 RCTs) and the vision symptoms that need same-day care
candidates.angle: Calm, numbers-first 'what's confirmed?' explainer for people already on tirzepatide. The FDA calls the risk 'potential' and the evidence has limits: the trial meta-analysis showed 6.4 vs 3.8 NAION events per 100,000 person-years. Sentinel found no significant increase vs SGLT-2 inhibitors but did find one vs DPP-4 inhibitors. Known NAION risk factors (smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea) overlap with the people these medicines help. Give an exact symptom card using the label's own wording (sudden, painless vision loss in one eye, often on waking; blurred or missing portions of vision; colour changes) → contact your prescriber or eye doctor promptly. Any decision to stop is made with the clinician; never tell viewers to stop. Weigh it against the established benefits for the right populations.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–5 days (news peak now; search for 'tirzepatide eyes' stays high for weeks as people ask their prescribers)
candidates.why_now: The FDA required class-wide Warnings and Precautions labeling on 9 Nov 2026. CNN, Reuters, AP, NBC, CBS, ABC, WSJ, WaPo, STAT, Sky and USA Today all covered it within 24 h. 'Ozempic blindness' is trending in Google GB (1,000+). Most coverage is semaglutide-first and alarm-led, so a tirzepatide-first calm explainer with the absolute numbers fills a clear gap. It's a body-worry topic, which is our best Shorts format.

evidence.signal: Covers tirzepatide, semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide and orforglipron. Warnings and Precautions section. 126 RCTs, 134,253 patients: 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years. Sentinel not elevated vs SGLT-2i.
FDA requires NAION warning across the GLP-1 receptor agonist class; referral to an ophthalmologist when suspected
FDA warns GLP-1 drugs carry potential risk of rare eye condition (9 Nov)
'ozempic blindness' 1,000+ searches, 10 Nov
'FDA adds GLP-1 vision loss warning, but evidence is mixed', a balanced framing gap

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and blurry vision: common, temporary changes vs the rare NAION warning signs, plus what the label says about diabetic retinopathy for people with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: An 'Is this normal?' body-worry companion to the NAION news. Many viewers will now worry about any blur. Separate the label's rare, sudden, one-eye, painless pattern from other eye symptoms that are worth raising at a routine visit. For people with type 2 diabetes and a history of retinopathy, the label advises monitoring. Give a clear 'call today' vs 'mention at your next appointment' split, and recommend regular eye exams. Every claim must be tied to label text, and nothing gets diagnosed.
keywords: when to see eye doctor GLP-1
candidates.why_now: The NAION warning will push a wave of 'is my blurry vision from tirzepatide?' searches over the next 1–2 weeks. Calm body-worry Shorts with tirzepatide in the title are our proven best format (median about 93).

evidence.signal: Label symptom list and risk factors for NAION; prompt ophthalmology evaluation

evidence.source: PubMed / J Korean Med Sci (2 Nov)
evidence.signal: Review of GLP-1 RA ocular safety and retinal outcomes
'Do Ozempic, Zepbound cause vision loss? New FDA warning explained': consumer question volume

candidates.topic: Strength training on tirzepatide, new Nature Medicine RCT (9 Nov): resistance exercise three times a week for 40 weeks cut lean-mass loss by about 25% vs usual activity (120 adults with overweight or obesity, 91% adherence)
candidates.angle: 'Will tirzepatide make me lose muscle?', answered with the first randomized trial done specifically on tirzepatide users. Say what it shows: on average, less lean tissue lost with supervised resistance training compared with usual activity, over 40 weeks. Then the practical part: what the training looked like and how to talk to your clinician before starting. It's a narrow, adjacent hook to Strength and Bones & Muscle, not a general protein or diet video. Keep the exact population, comparator and 'on average'.
keywords: how to keep muscle on tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (also feeds New Year resolution searches)
candidates.why_now: It was published 9 Nov in Nature Medicine and so far only the UWA press release and the NY Post '6-minute habit' story cover it. It's fresh randomized tirzepatide data, which fits the 13:00 lead slot. Strength has stalled and needs an adjacent video for suggested-video pickup, and muscle Shorts already reach 138.

evidence.signal: RCT: 120 adults on tirzepatide, resistance training 3×/week vs usual activity, 40 weeks; attenuated lean soft-tissue loss; 91% adherence

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol over the holidays: what the label and new research say (DOM target trial emulation of semaglutide and tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes, 3 Nov), no 'safe amount', and the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas
candidates.angle: 'Does tirzepatide change how drinking feels?' Holiday-season framing. The observational alcohol-outcome link is presented strictly as 'linked to'. Talk about the overlap with GI side effects and dehydration. Never give a safe amount. Add the hypoglycaemia caveat for anyone on insulin or a sulfonylurea, and the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: The new DOM paper (3 Nov) is out, and semaglutide alcohol and opioid addiction trials were announced 10 Nov (The Pharmacist). The holiday party season starts in 2 weeks. It's on the playbook's Lane A list.

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain on placebo from week 36 to 88, placebo still 9.9% below starting weight on average), plus habits that help
candidates.angle: An adjacent follow-up to our best-CTR video (Stopping, 8.44%). Regain isn't the same for everyone. Cover which habits the evidence supports for maintaining results (strength training, using the new tirzepatide RCT as the hook, protein, sleep, follow-up care), and why any change to the medicine is a conversation with the prescriber. No stopping or switching advice.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 pill for sleep apnea: orforglipron (Foundayo) Phase 3 ATTAIN-OSA cut breathing interruptions by 43.8% without CPAP and 27.5% with CPAP at 52 weeks vs placebo, alongside tirzepatide's existing sleep apnea approval
candidates.angle: A 'what's confirmed?' Short: tirzepatide (Zepbound) already has a US approval for moderate-to-severe OSA with obesity. Now a daily GLP-1 pill has Phase 3 results, but these are separate trials, not head-to-head, the data are company-reported and not yet peer-reviewed, and an FDA filing is planned. Don't suggest anyone can drop their CPAP; any change to it is a decision with their clinician.

Plain line: retatrutide isn't approved, and online 'research' products aren't the trial drug. Tie back to why weight loss can ease knee load. No buying information.
